items.title: 尽管 95% 的粉丝要求加入 AI 标签，VRChat 开发者还是拒绝加入，引发愤怒
items.summary: The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it woul

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/30/vrchat-devs-spark-outrage-over-ai-label-1793390533984.jpg

The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.

VRChat is a virtual hub where folks can gather to chat, make their own avatars, and create and play games together. It’s a fairly popular social platform that, perhaps unsurprisingly, is a hotbed for viral moments and hilarious content.
Also unsurprisingly, there’s been a sharp increase in AI-generated content in VRChat, to the point where fans are begging for some sort of distinction as to what has and hasn’t been made by humans.

In fact, the folks behind VRChat recently published a survey asking users for their feedback on the state of the platform. In that survey, “95% of survey respondents want some kind of label for AI usage,” as told in an official blog published on October 28.

Despite this overwhelming majority, the powers that be have decided against moving forward with an AI label, arguing that there’s simply too much disagreement among users as to what, exactly, should be done to delineate such content.

“We’re not adding an ‘AI-generated’ label or AI filters,” the devs said in the blog post. “While we think some creators would honestly label their content, we think others would try to pass off generative or assisted work as completely authored by hand. Likewise, we could see this creating ‘sleuthing’ behavior, where folks would attempt to sniff out ‘AI’ content or might harass other creators, even if they are genuinely not using any AI tools in their workflow. We think this potentially creates negative behavior spirals we don’t want to encourage.”
The statement continued, revealing that respondents gave “3,141 different combinations of labeling,”and that “no single combination was given by more than 10% of respondents.”
Essentially, the team at VRChat feels they need to “understand this a layer deeper before making any kneejerk decisions” — but their explanation hasn’t been well-received by fans.

On social media, dedicated VRChat users are speaking out against this decision, with one writing on X/Twitter, “Then what was the point of the survey if they’re not going to f**king use it to influence decisions?”
“95% of YOUR players said NO to AI content. That isn't a debatable margin,” another argued .
“The point of having a filter is because we do NOT want to see that content. They are FILTERS for a reason, bruh,” another exasperated user wrote .

Thus far, VRChat has made no official response to this outrage and is continuing to move forward with planned events, leaving users beside themselves as they work to make their voices heard by the platform.

items.title: 猩红沙漠：绘制迄今为止未知的评论
items.summary: After six hours with this beefy DLC, it seems to add even more to Crimson Desert’s buffet-style approach while

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/30/crimson-desert-charting-the-unknown-blogroll-01-1793388254836.jpg

Crimson Desert’s biggest strength is in the sheer volume of stuff it throws at you, allowing you to spend hundreds or even a thousand-plus hours doing everything from hunting animals with a bow to developing a gambling addiction at the tavern. So it’s not very surprising that Crimson Desert’s first paid DLC, called Charting the Unknown, prioritizes adding more on top of its already staggeringly large repertoire. So far, the interesting new activities that mostly focus on oceanic adventures are exactly as compelling as you’d hope, with ship-to-ship combat, underwater exploration, and romance options being among the list of new worthwhile features. On the other hand, existing activities that have added content, like the extra story missions, have mostly been uninspired retreads that don’t do anything to improve upon their established shortcomings. When Crimson Desert came out, I said that its content was a mile long and an inch deep, and for better or worse this DLC seems to say, “Here’s another half-mile.”

The most disappointing part of the DLC so far has been the additional story missions, which are only accessible once you’ve completed the base game’s already dense main story (a feat which only 10% of Steam players have done, judging by the achievements system). At least the handful of missions I’ve completed at this point have mostly served as an expanded epilogue of sorts, with Kliff fighting more difficult versions of old bosses from the existing story, and Damiane and Oongka fleshing out their less substantial stories as well.

I’m not far enough to know if any of these quests eventually become more interesting, but most of their objectives have been an oddly bland retracing of your steps, like going back to spend time with a familiar character and share a moment fishing together or arm wrestle someone to gather information as an apparent callback to an identical moment in the original story. I did get to a new stretch of the map just before getting distracted by the separate seafaring content, so hopefully this part of the DLC will pick up the pace, but so far it’s been about as unimpressive as I expected given the low bar for storytelling in Crimson Desert.

Much like the base content though, most of the effort seems to have been put into things that aren’t related to the story. Although most of my time has been spent dipping my toes into the water-based ship-crafting feature that’s the focus of this expansion, it feels like I’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg, with new resources to obtain, crewmates to hire, and even more activities to learn like harpooning fish and ship-to-ship combat before you can really begin your voyages properly.

It's going to take more time to fully engage with these new activities and judge whether or not they have the sea legs to keep me entertained for longer than a few hours, but at least right now I’m just impressed (yet again) by the fact that these systems exist in this adventure that’s already so damn packed with things to do. Gliding underwater on the back of a sea turtle and captaining your own pirate crew truly just feel completely bizarre in the context of Crimson Desert, and so far that’s been compelling enough to keep me moving forward even if some of the other added content isn’t great.

There’s still a ton I have to investigate, like additional base building and property management features, a challenging combat arena-style gauntlet, and my personal favorite – social links and romance mechanics for NPCs, which I’m very excited to check out once I’ve gotten my bearings (I’m just not ready to settle down yet, okay?!).
What I said about Crimson Desert

"There’s lots to love about this quirky, kitchen sink design, and I admire that it’s managed to pack a metric ton of unique mechanics and interesting areas into one package. But it takes work to dig your way through the thick layer of gunk that covers it all, and the mostly competent action-adventure game that’s buried beneath is only sometimes worth that effort." (March 20, 2026)
Score: 6
Read the full review

For all the stuff that’s been added, one thing that is the same since the last time I played is the number of bugs I’ve encountered in my brief time with the Charting the Unknown DLC. I’ve already had two hard crashes, one character wig out on me while I was trying to arm wrestle him (he was hilariously standing behind me during the match, arm bent unnaturally), and quite a few blurry or flickering textures that are impossible for me to not focus on during cutscenes. I’m still too early to tell if this is going to be a consistent issue, but in my time so far it’s been quite rocky from a technical perspective considering how much wonkiness I’ve encountered per hour played.

As expected with Crimson Desert, it’s going to take quite a bit of time to see and do enough to reach a definitive conclusion on Charting the Unknown, and I’m hopeful that the engaging and unexpected content that’s been added will be able to make up for some of the activities that feel like empty calories.

items.title: MTG Darkhold Destiny 4 Commander Deck Bundle：它们看起来好不好？
items.summary: Are MTG Darkhold Destiny's Commander bundles worth $299.96 or $639.96? Here's what's included and whether the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/18/magic-the-gathering-darkhold-destiny-commander-deck-bundle-1792353467227.jpg

Magic: The Gathering’s latest Marvel crossover is still nearly six months away, but Amazon preorders are already up for bundles containing four Darkhold Destiny Commander decks, though one is definitely more hefty in ptice than the other.
Whilst the standard four-deck bundle is currently selling for $299.96 on Amazon , the Collector’s Edition is going for $639.96 — both sold directly by the retailer, and launching on April 9, 2027.

Depending on which one you’re eyeing up, this works out to $74.99 or $159.99 each respectively. Understandably, that’s quite a high entry price and knock on potential trading card budgets, so you need to know exactly what you’re getting for your money, and whether that initial cost seems worthwhile, based on first impressions.
What comes in the Darkhold Destiny Commander Bundles?
No matter which price you pay, either Darkhold Destiny Commander bundle comes with the following decks: Strange Academy, Gods of Asgard, Midnight Sons, and Lords of Hel.
Each deck has 100 cards and is completely ready-to-play, containing 30 new-to-Magic Commander cards; that’s along with ten double-sided tokens, a deck box, and a strategy guide.

The difference between the two bundles is that the standard version comes with two Traditional Foil legendary creatures per deck; the Collector’s Editions, meanwhile, swap in Surge Foil treatments across all 100 cards.
Do these Commander decks actually look good?
Amongst the many preorders up for Darkhold Destiny in general, the Commander Decks definitely look at least interesting on paper.

For instance, with Strange Academy, Doctor Strange leads a white-blue-black blink deck that’s built around sending creatures out of play and bringing them back to make repeated use of their enter-the-battlefield effects, as pointed out by Wargamer . Since it’s quite a tried-and-tested strategy, there could be plenty of mileage with this deck, though it depends what the new cards will actually do effects-wise.

Meanwhile, Lords of Hel has Hela commanding a red-black token sacrifice deck; that’s another promising combo, but that depends on the payoff you get for sacrificing those creatures. In contrast, Thor’s red-green-white Gods of Asgard focuses on equipment and creatures with power four or more, whilst Blade’s white-black Midnight Sons revolves around Vampires, building life, and spending it to trigger abilities.

Considering the price, it is at least a relief to see that these are four Marvel-themed decks with more variety than doing the same thing. Plus, with the expansion itself, as we learned when it was announced , Darkhold Destiny is set to be the first Universes Beyond set building around an original story shared between Marvel and Wizards of the Coast.

On the other hand, until we see the full decklists, we can’t at least 100% determine whether all decks will be objectively good in the game’s meta when Darkhold Destiny comes out. That said, if you loved the original Marvel Super Heroes expansion and are excited to see more, it should be at least safe to pre-order the standard $299.96 bundle — and wait until further down the line to decide on the Collector’s Editions.

items.title: 刺猬被喷成蓝色看起来像索尼克后死了
items.summary: An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Seg

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2024/04/10/sonic-the-hedgehog-2-biplane-stance-1712785795787.jpg
An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog .

The heartbreaking story comes from West Yorkshire in the UK, where a male hedgehog was found with extensive chemical burns after being spray-painted blue by supposed vandals. The animal was discovered outside the Wakefield police station and subsequently brought to Castleford Hedgehog Rescue on Tuesday, October 27, for treatment.

Unfortunately, the poor critter didn’t make it. Local reports state that the spray paint literally burned through “several layers” of the hedgehog’s skin, to the point where it melted its spines, causing extreme pain.

29-year-old Beth Campbell, who operates the hedgehog rescue, says she tried everything in her power to help — but the pain was so severe that the defenseless animal literally “screamed himself to death.”

"I don't know how anyone could be so cruel to an animal. It is disgusting,” she told YorkshireLive. "I haven't seen anything as bad or as sad as this in a long time. …I'm glad he was brought in, as it meant at least we could ease his suffering and make him feel comfortable."

Campbell says the spray paint gave the hedgehog significant chemical burns that, in turn, triggered an infection on its now-exposed skin. This, along with potential poisoning from the chemicals in the spray paint, is what ultimately caused its death.

She also revealed that the hedgehog was suffering from a condition known as flystrike, which occurs when flies lay their eggs in animals’ open wounds or soft tissue, resulting in maggots that feast on their flesh. Spray paint aside, Campbell said that the critter would have likely undergone a "slow and ultimately and extremely painful death" in the wild.

On Facebook , the hedgehog rescued posted a heartwrenching tribute to the deceased hedgehog: “As a result of cruelty our poor boy has passed away. This has deeply affected our volunteers and myself as he laid screaming in pain, he was given the full amount of pain relief he could have," the group wrote.

“Rest peacefully little man, the way you were treated was horrific, we tried everything we possibly could to save you, but you were too precious for this cruel world. Pain free, running free across the rainbow bridge.”

Campbell said she plans to report the incident to police, but is unsure if any action will be taken, given the location where the animal was found. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and local police have not released a statement regarding the matter.

Hedgehogs are listed as a nearly threatened species globally and are classified as vulnerable for extinction within the UK. Populations of the animal have dropped between 30-75% since 2000, with expanding human activity impacting their ability to find food, shelter, and otherwise survive.

items.title: 育碧确认“没有其他《刺客信条》重制版正在积极开发中”
items.summary: Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resyn

others.title: 育碧目前正在暂停《刺客信条》重制版

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2022/09/16/ac-1-1663336669216.jpg
Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resynced anytime soon.

The publisher behind the history-hopping stealth-action franchise laid all its cards on the table in a lengthy update post yesterday. Considering that this year's Assassin's Creed 4 remake seemed to go off without a hitch when it launched in July, one might assume re-imaginings for other games are on the way – but that is not the case.

When spelling out where Assassin's Creed has been and where it's heading, Ubisoft plainly addressed desires for more re-imaginings in a section called 'What About Other Remakes?' It knows Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has fans chomping at the bit for more, but it doesn't sound like we'll be getting any more for a very long time.

"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," it said. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

Why not revisit older games? Black Flag has remained a beloved installment in the franchise even more than a decade after its original release, but fans have continued to clamor to revisit stories from games like the original Assassin's Creed , Assassin's Creed 2 , and Assassin's Creed 3 . As happy with Black Flag Resynced as Ubisoft is, the publisher admitted that returning to the West Indies took more than a little legwork.

"As our first-ever franchise remake, Resynced taught us a tremendous amount," it explained. "Taking on a game that holds such a special place in players' hearts brought both excitement and challenges. Rebuilding old systems from scratch, adding new elements that fit the experience, and balancing legacy with innovation was a massive undertaking. We're super proud of what the Resynced team delivered and how well it was received."

Unfortunately, we won't be donning Altair or Ezio's Assassin cloaks anytime soon. Still, just because no remakes are in development now, it doesn't mean there won't ever be an opportunity to return to fan-favorite worlds and stories.

"But don't mistake that for a closed door. Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back. That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted."

Of course, that doesn't mean the Creed is going anywhere. Ubisoft also acknowledged that its teams are "focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles," which includes projects fans "haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories." One of those is Codename Hexe , another game that it made sure to touch on in its update post . In May, the publisher said the plan was to deliver new games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Ghost Recon franchises over the course of the next few years .

IGN gave Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced a 9/10 review . We said, "More than just a shinier version of the same game you remember, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced brings what was already one of the best games in the series up to today’s standards." Its final major content update added New Game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more earlier this week.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI：原创乐谱现已开放预购
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Original Score is a three-hour compilation of new music from Justice, and it's availa

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/30/untitled-design-1793387100239.png

Grand Theft Auto: The Original Score is now available for preorder in vinyl and CD format . It’s by the Grammy Award-winning French electronic duo Justice, and it contains 30 tracks, including the songs “ Flower in a Hurricane ” and “ Pusher ." The album is set to release December 11 , which is nearly a month after GTA 6 the game comes out. Here’s everything you need to know to preorder it.
Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score - Vinyl (3 LP)
The vinyl edition comes in a 3LP set with UV gloss finish. Amazon has black vinyl, while Justice's storefront has it in a limited-edition clear vinyl.
Grand Theft Auto VI: The Original Soundtrack - CD
The CD version comes on two discs, in an intricate fold-out case featuring GTA 6 imagery.
GTA 6: The Original Score vs. GTA 6: The Album

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Original Score is a three-hour compilation of music primarily by Justice. It's not to be confused with Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , which features original songs by a variety of musicians.
Whichever format you choose, the album includes 30 songs, plus “a number of digital bonus tracks.” In total, the score includes three hours’ worth of material from the game.

So far, only two tracks from this album have been released. The first is “Flower in a Hurricane,” by Justice, featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, which is the song featured the launch trailer . The other song is “Pusher,” by Justice featuring the French DJ and record producer Gesaffelstein.

Where to Preorder GTA 6: The Album

content.v: I've made peace with our 2026 list and accepted that a few of my most anticipated releases may wind up on our new PC games 2027 calendar instead. items.title: 《星际迷航 Online》玩家举行公众守夜活动以哀悼帕特里克·斯图尔特
items.summary: In orbit and planetside, the MMO's player base is honoring its most-loved captain.

others.title: 《星际迷航 Online》玩家组成银河级仪仗队向皮卡德船长演员帕特里克·斯图尔特爵士致敬
《星际迷航》和《X 战警》传奇演员帕特里克·斯图尔特去世

content.v: Yesterday, the world received the sad news that legendary stage and screen actor Patrick Stewart had died at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia." His passing has triggered an internet-wide celebration of his life—particularly from Star Trek fans honoring his tenure as The Next Generation's Captain Jean-Luc Picard.

While countless social media posts have already been penned in Stewart's memory, a subset of Trekkies are grieving together in the shared virtual spaces of Star Trek Online, the modest MMO that's still keeping the lights on 16 years after its 2010 launch. With orbital starship flotillas and starbase torchlight vigils, STO's humble playerbase is turning out to mourn one of its most beloved figures—just as it had done earlier this week for the death of Walter Koenig .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/viBxuMQH4mrAHsPoHk8sBC-1920-80.jpg

Recalling the faint memories of having made my own STO account in prior years, I logged in to join in that mourning myself—at which point I discovered that I'd never finished the tutorial questline, and that the intervening years' updates to the new player experience had broken my character's ability to progress. But after an hour of building a fresh, new cadet-turned-captain and getting my space legs by scanning radiation clouds and blowing up a collection of Borg shapes, I was free to head Earthward to participate in players' impromptu memorial gatherings.

Once I arrived in the Sol system, it didn't take much looking. I was welcomed into Earth orbit by an assembly of player-captained Galaxy-class exploration cruisers, the same class of starship as the USS Enterprise-D that Picard captained in The Next Generation. The vessels arranged in Stewart's honor included names like the USS Remembrance, the USS ForEverPicard, the USS Champion—and the USS Purple Enterprize, which was like The Enterprise, except purple.

After surveying the fleet, I beamed aboard the Earth Spacedock, the in-game faction hub for Federation players. There, ringed around a large Starfleet seal, was a gathering of players all holding aloft torches—an emote the game provides for honoring "absent friends." It was just one of a number of concurrent player memorials happening across the Spacedock's map instances, seven of which were either full or near capacity when I was online.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Sx5WrtURoxqbwkGzn7puhM-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ncHNTh75KFjgezh5BNny6V-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/m6GQAoSB5eD3DsUgCQuRUZ-1920-80.jpg

It was a touching scene, even if one of my fellow mourners was a tiny Ferengi lad named "Shmunguss" and—in true MMO fashion—an argument about atheism broke out in the zone chat. But the tension was diffused by one player offering a farewell wish that "may the Force be with you, Gandalf." Close enough.

From the Spacedock, I headed planetside to the Starfleet Academy grounds, where multiple instances were likewise packed with players commemorating Stewart's passing. In my instance, the torchlight vigil was even more solemn than the one taking place in orbit. One user—named Picard, and customized to match—had volunteered as a sort of body-vessel for the player base's collective grief.

At rank 63, the character evidently hadn't been made with this purpose in mind. But they stood still and silent before a crowd of sorrowful Star Trek fans. Many were content with holding their torches; some—like one player dressed like a Napoleonic admiral—saluted. Others shared Picard quotes, or scraps of Shakespearean soliloquies. One character, a Vulcan, diligently progressed through every available emote that could serve as an expression of anguish.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/zvc65fKxFVNemaRcNVkZwf-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FrSJM7nb4DQtKCZ9fwQM6i-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/UYtxst3WRyy6XJKoGXBiWk-1920-80.jpg
Judging from the untranslated text that accompanied his emotes, he was a Vulcan who hailed from Germany.

Between the Galaxy-class cruisers massed in orbit, the Spacedock tributes, and the Academy vigils, the hundreds of users gathering to offer their farewells represents a substantial portion of the 1,500 or so STO players online on Steam at time of writing. Star Trek Online might not be topping charts in 2026, but it can offer its players a place to come together and mourn the man who brought their captain to life. For an MMO at its age, maybe that's the sort of thing that matters most.

items.title: Reddit 很快就会要求你登录，可能是因为人工智能概述
items.summary: Over the years, Reddit has become almost the default message board for most of the internet, and as such house

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2023/06/16/reddit-1686939713860.png

Over the years, Reddit has become almost the default message board for most of the internet, and as such, houses answers to thousands of questions that anyone could access, even without an account. However, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman has suggested that most of Reddit will end up locked behind a login screen.

In a post simply titled 'About that login screen,' Huffman talks about his decision to turn Reddit into a "primarily logged-in experience." And, in true Reddit fashion, he also includes a TL;DR, where he says, "We’re making the change because it’s better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data. And we can do this while continuing to ensure user privacy." But I suspect that this all leads back to Google's AI overviews.

The first section of Huffman's long post is all about personalization, and it sounds like they're going to use your account to build a personal algorithm, which will show you more of the content that you're interested in. That is extremely normal for any website in 2026. According to the post, "Our goal is to help you find what’s most relevant to you and drive the community, connection and belonging that makes Reddit, Reddit."
But in the next section, Huffman says a big part of the decision is to 'protect our business and meet regulations.'

He clarifies, saying, "The first is that access to Reddit's data corpus has to be intentional. Today, the vast majority of unauthorized access to Reddit (basically the scraping and stealing of Reddit’s data) happens through our logged-out experiences. We will continue licensing our corpus intentionally, but those commercial deals come with guardrails that protect our users and our business. Any commercial deals give us the right to say what the data can and can't be used for and how it's presented. Without those guardrails and that intentionality, we can't control who has access to Reddit data, where things go or what they're used for."

It's not hard to see why Reddit would want to combat unauthorized scraping of its content. I know, personally, I've Googled questions I've needed answers to, only to get a bunch of answers in Google's AI overview that are essentially ripped straight from Reddit. It's in Reddit's best interest, then, to stop that from happening.

In a letter shared with shareholders , Huffman said that, "Our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter. The biggest impact was on logged-out and web traffic." Specifically, Huffman says, "During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week." And it doesn't take much of a stretch to connect that to AI overviews.

However, it does seem like there will be some limitations to Reddit's logged-in-only experience. According to the blog, the front page of Reddit will still be accessible without logging in, and you should be able to click on a direct Reddit link shared from a friend, and access that thread. But I get the impression that this system is still in the very early days, and the details of how exactly it'll work will emerge in the next few months.

Huffman says the next step will be "to test this in select markets outside the U.S. in the coming months." And, based on those tests, Reddit will likely decide which content is going to be available for the general audience and which content is going to be walled off behind an account.

This isn't the first time in recent years that Reddit has drastically changed the way the website is run. Just last year, Reddit changed its mod removal policy, after Huffman suggested the company would do so back in 2023. And, earlier, Reddit also made access to its API for third-party apps more expensive in 2023.

items.title: “如果你没有太多期望就更好了”——神谷秀树谈《大神》续集
items.summary: IGN got the chance to bend Hideki Kamiya’s ear about the long-awaited Okami sequel at Lucca Comics and Games F

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/02/14/okamisequel-directsequel-blogroll-1739534302291.jpg

IGN got the chance to bend Hideki Kamiya’s ear about the long-awaited Okami sequel at Lucca Comics and Games Festival 2026, where he shed some light on his creative process and addressed fans’ expectations about the upcoming title.

In December 2024 — almost 20 years after Okami was first released — fans of Clover Studio's critically acclaimed, cult-classic game were treated to news they never could’ve expected: a proper sequel was being made , led by the game’s original director, Hideki Kamiya.

Kamiya and Clovers, his new studio comprised of former Clover staff and industry veterans, are hard at work creating Amaterasu’s next adventure. And while he can’t say much about the project just yet, he did give us a smidge more insight about what the team has been cooking up over the last two years.

It’s safe to say Kamiya is keenly aware of players’ high expectations for the Okami sequel. It’s a tear-jerkingly beautiful game that’s been marinating in fans’ hearts and minds for two decades at this point, after all. But just as he approached the first game, he is once again planning to make an experience that appeals to both seasoned players and greenhorns alike.

“I created the first chapter of Okami keeping in mind that what I wanted to do was create a gaming experience that would be satisfying to relative beginners,” he told us via a translator, referencing Okami’s “sequence of commands for attacks.”

“When I created the plane sequences for Bayonetta — or even the game, itself — I had in mind players who were a little more experienced, obviously. Now that I’m making a second chapter of Okami, I’m going back to think about the more inexperienced or relatively new players. I still want to make it enjoyable for them, too,” he explained.

Kamiya is no stranger to kickstarting new franchises or creating sequels for pre-existing properties. (He did direct Resident Evil 2 , after all.) But given the amount of hype from hardcore fans for the Okami sequel, he’s urging players to temper their expectations.

“[The Okami sequel] has become a sort of mission for me, because before, when I created a new game, I had no expectation from the public, of course. It was something completely new and, in a sense, unexpected. Now that I’ve created sequels, the expectation from the public has grown quite a lot, and I feel that. It’s better if you don’t have many expectations.”

When it comes to this new project, Kamiya doesn’t feel that his creative process has necessarily changed in the last 20 years. Instead, he says that he’s gained a sixth sense of a sort, where he can tell he’s going to make a mistake before it actually happens. (Which, I must admit, sounds like an especially useful skill to have.)

“As far as I can see, nothing has changed,” he mused when asked about how his process has evolved over the years. “The only thing I think is that, since I’ve made so many mistakes during my career, now, when I feel like I’m approaching a mistake, I can feel it beforehand. That’s the difference from then and now.”

Perhaps unsurprisingly, he couldn’t say much more about the Okami sequel. But what we did learn is that, just like its predecessor, this game will be accessible to newer players and seasoned gamers alike, appealing to both demographics just as the first one did.

For more Okami sequel news, you can check out IGN’s interview from early 2025 when we flew to Japan to chat with Kamiya, Kiyohiko Sakata, and Yoshiaki Hirabayashi, who told us that the next Okami game is a direct continuation from the first and not a side-story like Okamiden was.

items.title: 《战争机器：E-Day》据称制作成本达 5 亿美元，但声称仅售出 40 万份
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly cost $500 million to make, amid claims it has sold just over 400,000 copies.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/01/btfiuoeldu6mkzuez7e008xhvd1icgg-jcb-u5aiuoy-1790813782471.jpeg
Gears of War: E-Day reportedly cost $500 million to make, amid claims it has sold just over 400,000 copies.

The Coalition’s action game launched on Xbox Series X and S and PC only, after Microsoft went down the console exclusive route following Asha Sharma’s arrival as Xbox CEO. As a Microsoft Studios game, E-Day also launched day one on subscription service, Xbox Game Pass.

This week, The Verge reported that E-Day had sold over 400,000 copies across console and PC. That’s a poor sales figure for any triple-A video game of Gears of War’s scope and prestige, but it could be an even worse commercial situation for Microsoft and The Coalition, given the extraordinary budget for E-Day.
Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier rubber-stamped recent reports about E-Day’s budget in a video expanding on the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and the closure of BioWare.

“We just saw Gears of War: E-Day cost $500 million to Xbox. And that is a real number. That is real,” Schreier said. “That's what we're looking at here. That's what [AAA] games cost to make, especially in North America these days. And it’s driving these game companies to make layoffs, to do cost-cutting, to move development outside North America in a lot of cases, and to focus only on the biggest franchises that have as little risk as possible.”

The $500 million figure for E-Day was first reported by Kotaku , which said it was before marketing costs. IGN asked Microsoft for comment at the time, but it has yet to respond. It makes E-Day one of the most expensive video games ever made, and comes in at double the cost of some of its rivals. Bungie's recently released extraction shooter, Marathon, reportedly had a budget of over $250 million , for example. Concord's initial development deal was around $200 million, according to a report by Kotaku . In 2023, documents submitted as part of the Xbox Federal Trade Commission case accidentally revealed The Last of Us: Part II and Horizon Forbidden West each cost more than $200 million to develop . Last year, the astronomical development budgets of the Call of Duty games were revealed for the first time after a court document confirmed Activision pumped $700 million into Black Ops Cold War alone, although that was over the shooter's life cycle.

On October 13, a week after E-Day’s official release date, Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliott estimated that the game had generated $42.1 million in revenue, having sold 311,000 copies across Steam and Xbox. He also pointed to a boost to Game Pass subscriptions that appears to have been the result of E-Day’s release, although lamented the lack of a PS5 version, which may have generated increased revenue.

One question Microsoft may have when it comes to Gears is the impact on Game Pass. Has it made a big enough impact on the subscription service to offset disappointing sales revenue? With a budget in the $500 million range, can Gears of War: E-Day ever be considered profitable?

Discussing Xbox’s ongoing financial struggles this week, Sharma pointed to Minecraft and World of Warcraft Forever as setting records, and the critical acclaim Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 had enjoyed. No mention was made of Gears of War: E-Day .

What does this all mean for the future of the franchise? Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.

Eurogamer had reported on internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda.

The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently told the BBC that success for E-Day goes beyond sales, saying: "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware.”

items.title: Zelda Producer 'Nervous' About Fan Reception to Ocarina of Time Remake
items.summary: Eiji Aonuma, the longtime producer of The Legend of Zelda franchise at Nintendo, is preparing to launch the hi

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/30/zelda-1793383652173.avif

Eiji Aonuma, the longtime producer of The Legend of Zelda franchise at Nintendo, is preparing to launch the highly anticipated remake of 1996's seminal The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time next week. And after so many years and so many Zelda games, you'd think it was routine for him. But it turns out he's nervous this time.

"I'm all nervous about releasing the remake of 'Ocarina' because I don't know how it's going to turn out, I can't stop thinking about it," he told AFP at a press event in Paris. The stakes are certainly a bit different this time around, as Aonuma and his team undertook the dauting task of remaking what many regard to be one of the greatest games of all time, as opposed to every other Zelda game they've made (well, almost ) that is an original work.

As AFP notes, the original Ocarina of Time was the first project Aonuma worked on with legendary Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto. Now, he and his team are remaking it, and after we got to play it, we found it to be a bit more different than you might think if you're a veteran of the original. We also had someone who never played the original try it out if you're curious as to his impressions. Aonuma also talked about how some members of his team had never played the original – and he thinks that's a good thing.

If IGN metrics are anything to go by, Aonuma-san has nothing to be nervous about next week. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is IGN's second-highest-performing preview of the year so far (after, you guessed it, our preview of GTA 6 ). However, on our YouTube channel, it is #1 by a mile with over 1.8 million views.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake will be released on November 5. Stay tuned for IGN's review coverage, and in case you need to jog your memory or you're a first-time player, our game help guide is here for you.

But to get this perfect ending, besides following the main quest, you have to complete a variety of side activities.

The cut-off for completion seems quite generous—though Inanis implies there's a point of no return just as you enter the Mirage Estate, I completed some of these steps later and I was fine. Here's what you need to do

items.summary: A Daedalic adventure classic is free on GOG

others.title: Inspired by Classic FromSoftware, Queen's Domain Looks a Fascinating PS5 Adventure

content.v: We previewed A New Beginning , a Daedalic point-and-click adventure about saving the world from environmental catastrophe, all the way back in 2011, and it seemed promising: "Neither preachy nor educational," despite its ecological angle, but "pure sci-fi, involving a clash between one magic power-source that nukes the Earth, and a race to get it replaced with another magic one that turns simple algae into the ultimate fuel." A good bit of time-travel, too. That's always fun.

That promise paid off in the final release—not one of Daedalic's most memorable games, but a solid point-and-clicker from a studio that was at the time beginning to establish itself as one of the masters of the genre. And all of this is relevant to you because A New Beginning: Final Cut is now free on GOG.

I'm not sure why it's free, exactly: The giveaway isn't explicitly connected to GOG's currently-underway 18 th Anniversary Sale (which is worth checking out in its own right, as always there are some very cheap deals to be had), nor is A New Beginning what I'd call a Halloween-themed game—although the prospect of ecological collapse driven by climate change that humanity seems studiously determined to ignore is pretty horrifying, come to think of it.
But on the other hand, who cares, because it's free: Just hit the giveaway link on GOG's front page and it's yours. You've got until November 2 to make the grab.

items.title: 这个残酷的《辐射 4》恐怖模组将联邦变成了寂静岭
items.summary: Introduce Pyramid Head and friends to the Boston suburbs in Whispering Hills.

content.v: Fallout 4's overworld was always missing something that the other 3D wastelands in the series offered me: a sense of bleakness and danger. There are areas of the map, like the Glowing Sea, that managed to dial up the oppression. But the unforgiving horror mod Whispering Hills makes the whole region eerie and mysterious. And I honestly love that.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N5WXFQSCttV6Am7CopwTzd-1920-80.png
This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 .

My playthrough started the same way as vanilla Fallout 4, with a tableau of mid-Century suburban domestic bliss interrupted by a tense run to Vault 111. But from there, I almost started to think my hard drive was haunted. The post-nuclear world has been reimagined with constant, dense fog and occasional torrential rain that limit your view distance to only a handful of yards.

It reminded me of how Morrowind used its limited view distance to make Vvardenfell feel much bigger than it was, even if at the time it was also a technical necessity. Part of the problem with the Commonwealth overworld in unmodded Fallout 4 is that it's relatively flat and mostly green, so a lot of it feels very same-y. You can look off into the distance and not see anything so dramatic as the Nevada mountains or Washington DC's monuments. But when so much of the surrounding area is obscured, these gentle, rolling hills are suddenly quite effective at making my spine tingle.

The basic premise of Whispering Hills is similar to the base game. Your son Shaun was taken, and you have to find him. But this time, it sounds like he's been abducted by some kind of cult. I immediately ran into a mysterious man whose daughter had also been taken with a tip to go to the town of Whispering Hills to investigate. The locale itself is modeled on Centralia, PA, which was used as a reference for the live action Silent Hill movie and also happens to fit in quite well with the rural New England aesthetic of Fallout 4.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/k68UZbLLVd48MBPT3Kuque-1920-80.jpg

You won't be able to simply walk there, however. The first quest sends you to the Dunwich Borers dungeon, which is the site of one of the most memorable horror quests from the base game. And along the way, I could already tell something was very wrong. New enemies taken from and inspired by horror games and internet creepypastas show up alongside the usual raiders and mutants. Particularly upsetting was a towering Sirenhead who seemed to be broadcasting the distressed calls of a child Shaun searching for his mommy and daddy to lure me in.

Fair warning that this is a very tough mod to survive in starting as a fresh character. The enemies hit very hard, and some of them can soak a lot of damage, too. Sirenhead even managed to shrug off a mini nuke and send me running for the hills. I didn't bother to go progress the main quest long enough to get power armor, but I'd recommend at least levelling up a little bit in the open world before taking on Whispering Hills itself.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/p7vQxkvscSw8AEqsWwLsCe-1920-80.jpg
Journey to Hell
VATS is also disabled from here on out, with a scrawled note somewhat comedically explaining that the whole game mechanic was part of some kind of mass delusion.

After fighting my way through the usual bandits in Dunwich Borers and unsealing that foreboding chained door, I started to realize just how deep this descent was going to go. The feral ghouls from the vanilla version are replaced by Eyeless Ones with hooks for hands who are completely blind, but don't care at all about the light sources that serve as a boon in the vanilla quest. And upon reaching what would have been the end of the dungeon in an unmodded world, I was presented with another red door, and a notice that all of my items would be taken away if I entered it.

Things get absolutely terrifying and surreal from here. You can keep your levels and perks, but you don't gain any XP for killing enemies past the point of no return, and are given only rags and an automatic pistol with a limited amount of ammo to defend yourself. It's not even nearly enough to kill all the enemies down here, so stealth and running become essential. VATS is also disabled from here on out, with a scrawled note somewhat comedically explaining that the whole game mechanic was part of some kind of mass delusion.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/AixrKoau6bTxJRSELBU9Ye-1920-80.jpg

The lighting and sound design in these segments are very effective at selling the idea that we're not in Massachusetts anymore, with grisly tableaus of hanged cadavers and creepy radio broadcasts insisting you turn around only to see… nothing. The enemies are quite a bit tougher, too. At level four, some of them could kill me in only two hits, with the likes of mumblers and Silent Hill's horrible nurses joining the cast.

Throughout, themes of parenthood are laid on thick. You might see a rocking cradle in an inaccessible area behind grimy prison bars. Some of the enemies make distorted crying sounds. I haven't finished the mod's five chapters yet, but knowing how Silent Hill games tend to play out, it definitely seems like we're not going to find Shaun as an older man leading a science institute.

And at the deepest part of this charnel house, down a rusty set of stairs, you discover Shaun's rattle. And that's when he shows up. Pyramid Head in all his unholy glory will pursue you as you backtrack through the level to escape. I found this section to be particularly punishing, to the point that it's almost not that fun, at least at low level. But if you manage to make it out, the town of Whispering Hills and its unfolding story are your reward.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ScVFb5VPKVY5febzKDZeKe-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LqP4EnWuYEEAeZwL6MKiwe-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/og8hChfVtJkEV2SJrRHpve-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/tGHj3cMPPJnW6XSPyEYYqe-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/p4p8krie5UiDwtmDycMnve-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/j4PqRk74bZ9z2tnbUxmpVe-1920-80.jpg

Pyramid Head doesn't just stick to the modded areas. Once you have the rattle in hand, he can randomly appear even if you return to the Commonwealth. The only way to get him to stop pursuing you is to return the rattle to where you found it in the depths of Hell. And unsurprisingly, he doesn't seem to care much about any kind of laser beam or nuclear weapon you might throw at him. I could at least see Sirenhead's health going down, slowly. Our polyhedral buddy simply seems immune to all damage, leaving escape as the only recourse.

Overall, I love what Whispering Hills does to the default overworld. I do think some of the linear Hell segments are actually too hard to be scary. The problem is, dying over and over sort of inoculates you to the illusion horror games seek to create, and simply hoping I have enough AP to sprint past enemies I can't kill without too many of them hitting me feels random and isn't especially compelling.

But if you're looking for a spooky Halloween experience that turns a familiar game world into something deeply cursed and wrong, simply exploring the Commonwealth with Whispering Hills' diabolical changes is worth your time.

items.title: “我们表现得好像万圣节是我们的”：度过恐怖季节的最佳方式是在《Outlast Trials》的西尼亚拉设施内
items.summary: What better way to celebrate Halloween than by giving yourself nightmares?

content.v: I like to manifest Halloween year-round, what with my favourite pastimes being horror games, movies, and books—oh, and Dressmaker currently. So when Halloween actually falls upon me I like to make it something special—crack out the real horrifying stuff that'll hit even harder. One series that's always on my list is Outlast thanks to its next-level gore and perfect scares, plus if I want to drag my friends into a shared nightmare there's The Outlast Trials for all to enjoy.

"Halloween has always been—even going back to the first Outlast—one of our biggest months, and it definitely kickstarts the biggest part of the year, which is October, November, and the holidays," Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin tells me. "Those are usually the best months of the year in terms of sales. We don't control what other studios do, obviously, but we act as if Halloween is ours."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3Se6KyGzL6weHnyPfFBWKB-1920-80.jpg

This year Red Barrels decided to celebrate the spooky season with a huge sale to encourage new players to enter the Sinyala Facility and give The Outlast Trials a try over the spookiest month of the year. And it worked, way beyond what they'd hoped for: The game's concurrent player count on Steam ended up capping out at 147,955 players, a hugely impressive feat for a horror game that's over three years.

"We knew with that 90% sale we'd get a lot of new players, but we didn't expect that many," Morin says. "That first week of October was pretty insane. Every day I was waking up checking the numbers, thinking okay, that's probably going to be the top, and then it's gonna start to go down, but every day it kept going higher and higher.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MsE8jojKeoSV2rcpoY4DdK-1920-80.png

"Obviously after the sale it trickled down a little bit, but hopefully it's gonna stabilise at a much higher level than what we had before. But yeah, it's pretty satisfying to see that after being out for more than three years, the game still finds a new audience. And it's very satisfying to watch all these people play the game and suffer."

That they will. The Outlast Trials is still the scariest multiplayer horror game there is. Usually adding other players to a horror game will dampen the experience, whether that be because it becomes simply too funny to jump at or things just aren't as scary when you have your friends by your side. And while I've certainly laughed in The Outlast Trials it's usually a frantic nervous laugh that's triggered when I see some naked goliath barrelling towards an unsuspecting teammate.

But experiencing collective trauma with your friends isn't the only reason to play The Outlast Trials over Halloween: there's also a new event. The whole gist of The Outlast Trials is that you and your mates are stuck in a Murkoff testing facility, the Sinyala Facility, where everyone is forced to undergo weird and painful experiments. The goal, naturally, is escape, which is usually impossible—but right now, in this new event, it's actually attainable.

"There's the escape going on," Morin explains. "So for the first time in like a year, I think, there is a way to escape the facility—we made a communal event. People had to help out our character Amelia make the escape happen, and that's happened. I think on Sunday night they completed the task, and so since Sunday night, players have been able to escape. So now's the time because it's not going to last forever. Murkoff is always watching."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dmLfcTEceHMYUpsciYxiDT-1920-80.jpg

items.title: 漫步者 G5 Max 无线游戏耳机评测
items.summary: Lightweight, long-lasting, but lacking.

content.v: In the world of wireless gaming headsets, there's one spec that draws me in like a moth to a flame: battery life. Particularly 100-hour+ battery life. Wireless cans have come a long way in the last decade, but plugging them in all the time is an annoyance. If I can get away with multiple days without messing around with a cable, I usually will.

Which brings me to the Edifier G5 Max . Or the Edifier Hecate G5 Max, if you believe the writing on the box. It's got an astonishing "are you really sure" battery life spec of 305-hours, which meant I had to give it a look.

And now I've got one in my hands, I can confirm the battery life is impressive. Only the original HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless comes close. But the G5 Max, for its $150 / $160 price tag, isn't quite the full ticket in other departments.

For one, it comes with a remarkably boxy default sound profile, so you'll want to do some EQ tweaking in the software to sweeten it up. That's usually no big deal—except the EQ presets are as blunt as a hammer, so you'll need to play around with the sliders yourself if you want to get the most out of it. The 53 mm composite drivers are actually fairly decent once they've been fiddled with, but this is a set that massively benefits from some user assistance.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/uChRpFdiR9Fsap5himBPwP-1920-80.jpg

And for two, it doesn't have "$150 gaming headset" characteristics. This is a very light set of cans, coming in at just 305 grams. Light is good, but shiny, tippy-tappy ear cup plastics are not. It also looks a bit like a Power Ranger's codpiece, which will probably split the room.

The clamping force is also very light, to the point where it wants to slip around on my head, and the earpads feel a touch baggy. It's comfy, sure—but I do have reservations as to how long it will last.

$150 is premium pricing. Does this look, feel, and sound like a premium gaming headset? No, not really. Oh, and the multiple microphones are below par, too. The G5 Max has some good things going for it, but for this sort of cash? I think it lands a little wide of the mark.
Buy if...
✅ You want massive battery life: 305 hours worth, says Edifier. I can well believe it, as I've still not managed to drain it to zero after several weeks of on/off testing.
Don't buy if...

❌ You're not prepared to dive into the settings: Out of the box, the G5 Max has a disappointingly boxy sound profile. The software EQ presets are poor, so you'll need to get down and dirty with the options to coax it around. ❌ You want a good microphone: This one is dull, slightly muffled, and difficult to tweak, even if Edifier has thrown the kitchen sink at it in terms of software options.
Edifier G5 Max features
Operating principle
Closed back
Connectivity
2.4 GHz wireless via USB Type-A/Type-C dongle, Bluetooth 6.0, USB Type-C wired
Drivers
53 mm composite, titanium coated
Frequency response
Mic
Twin built-in ENC mics, detachable 9.75 mm unidirectional boom mic
Battery life
305-hour
Weight
Price

The Edifier G5 Max is a wireless gaming headset that tips the scales at just 305 grams. That's all the more impressive when combined with the battery life, which maxes out at a stated 305-hours. I have no idea why those specs line up the way they do, but it's a pleasing symmetry at the very least.

In terms of drivers, we're looking at a pair of 53 mm composite, titanium-coated units with a frequency response of 20,000 - 40,000 Hz. Connectivity options come in the form of a 2.4 GHz wireless dongle (with a nifty little switchable USB Type-C or Type-A plug design), a USB Type-C connection proper, and Bluetooth 6.0.

Add THX Spatial Audio+ support and up to 96 kHz/24-bit wired playback, along with support for the LHDC 5.0 codec for Bluetooth low-latency connectivity, and you've got a pretty fully-featured specs sheet. Microphones come in the form of a removable boom mic and two built-in units nestled deep within the internals.
Edifier G5 Max ergonomics
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N5tgeCpAYqykVseDmtcEaE-1920-80.jpg

Let's start with the good. The G5's headband is remarkably thick and squidgey, which feels very pleasant atop my head. The ear cup armature is solid metal, and has a slightly industrial feel to it that suggests it might last.

It's also very light, which means wearing the G5 Max for long periods is no issue at all. That being said, the earpads do give me pause for thought. They're a touch baggy, and while the material covering them is very soft and comfortable, it does seem a little fragile.

The clamping force is also very light. On the one hand, this is good for comfort. On the other, this headset has slipped from my dome more than once while moving around. Differing head sizes will end up with differing experiences here, but the G5 is light-touch enough to make itself an annoyance on occasion.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WEMFrS49NZ9vnd4eaEbdFY-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/DQcRZPDioC3mXVG2e5HgAM-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/XTd5vNEAdANSgtCdfYPH3M-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Gcua6fJ2CCssejKXaKcx7M-1920-80.jpg

The controls are a bit tinny, too. Combined with the clattering plastics used on the outside of the ear cups, this makes the whole endeavour feel a little cheap when you're adjusting it. And let's face it, at $150, this headset really isn't. Cheap, I mean.

Still, it's very comfortable when you're in a standard gaming position in front of your PC. Despite the Bluetooth 6.0 connection, though, I'm not sure I'd risk the whole affair slipping from my head while I was outside.
Edifier G5 Max sound
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/emrTSDWpnzbKXjSGVwfr5U-1920-80.jpg

If you simply plug in and go with the Edifier G5 Max, prepare yourself for a very boxy sound profile. While that might be advantageous in certain competitive gaming situations, it's not particularly nice to listen to for everyday usage.

You can tweak the EQ of this set within the Edifier Hecate app. Unfortunately, the audio presets it comes with are seriously heavy-handed. There are a handful of options for specific games (most of which boost the upper mids and treble to ear-aching levels while eschewing bass almost entirely), while the "bass" music preset itself lives up to its name:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YYxzm8ALRbPSk7pWdEZ9RK-1920-80.jpg

Holy hell, Batman, this looks like a 12-year-old's first headset EQ. Switching between all of the different options, I couldn't find one that worked well with the 53 mm drivers to create a balanced sound. Luckily, a little home tweaking can improve the sound profile considerably.

Basic stuff. A little bass boost from neutral, a small 200-300 Hz dip, a little push at the top end to sweeten up the treble. These 53 mm drivers need some work to sound their best, which is unfortunate.
Be prepared to break out the toolbox to warm the drivers up.

I would imagine that most gamers buying a $150 headset would expect it to sound lovely straight from the box, or at least be able to tweak it towards something halfway-pleasant without fiddling with the EQ beyond the given presets.

What the drivers are good at, though, is detail. Multiplayer shooter fans will appreciate their footstep-reproducing ways, and the positioning is very good, particularly with the spatial audio setting engaged. For everything else, though, be prepared to break out the toolbox to warm them up.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/EixU49vAUuCBqFYkYEocEa-1920-80.jpg

As for the microphone(s), they're also disappointing. The built-in units are dedicated to the Bluetooth connection and sound like every other internal set I've ever tested—hollow, but good enough to use in a pinch. Plug in the boom mic, though, and you get… well, it doesn't improve things much.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/R2q6UoSchmbjp7Cp2jwkaR-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/AUd7ESCEDrtDJd5dCJoksn-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ULfJpDkD5Sf8vMZjHQiWe7-1920-80.jpg

items.title: Struggling To Buy Magic’s Foundations Commander Decks? Wizards Confirms Reprints Are Likely
items.summary: Looking for a way to get the Foundations Commander Decks? Wizards of the Coast has confirmed to IGN that they'

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/16/foundations-new-commander-decks-ign-back-in-stock-1792148110129.png
Magic’s new sets are great, but one of the most impressive (and surprising) products of the year has been the Foundations Commander decks.

The five mono-colored preconstructed offerings have just started to sneak back down closer to MSRP , but with markups across the board and some (usually the mono-green Tramplesaurus Rex deck) still hard to find, we reached out to Wizards of the Coast to confirm what the state of play with additional printings would be.
Foundations Commander Decks To Be Evergreen
Brandon Kreines, game producer on Magic: The Gathering at Wizards of the Coast, had good news for fans looking to grab each of the precons.
“The new Foundations Commander Decks are definitely intended to be an evergreen offering,” Kreines explained.
“We can’t commit to specifics, but if players are as excited about these decks as we are, they should expect to see them get reprinted so they can be used as an introduction point into Commander.”

That’s good news for just about everyone. After all, if you want to get into Commander, you’ll want to do it for MSRP where possible, and while some decks have been marked up to over double what they should cost, more printings will mean a drop in price.

It’s also worth considering that there are no new cards in any of these decks. As a starter product, they offer a cohesive game plan in your color choice, but the more they’re printed, the more resellers will need to look elsewhere for their margins.

As we said back when these were announced, Starter Decks for Commander are not a new notion, but they’ve not been printed in so long that those ones climbed in price in the years since. If a reprint is coming, then we can likely expect more new players to the hobby which, in turn, benefits all of us.
For more on Magic: The Gathering, be sure to check out Reality Fracture’s most expensive cards , as well as all we know about the Warhammer 40K Commander decks seeing a reprint at long last .

items.title: EA 刚刚搁置了一个神秘的模拟人生项目——这对玩家来说可能是个好消息
items.summary: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that

content.v: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short . But things are feeling especially grim after EA trotted out two beloved franchises--Mass Effect and Dragon Age--for what amounted to a public execution via the announcement that BioWare has been shuttered .

This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims.

In the same breath it announced the end of BioWare, EA also reaffirmed its commitment to Apex Legends, Skate, and The Sims franchises. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. If EA is willing to pull the plug on legacy franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, where does that leave its other franchises, like The Sims 4 ?
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SimsFamily.png?w=636

According to EA, Sims fans need not worry, as the company is committed to "focusing on the long-term potential of The Sims." Apparently, focusing on that long-term potential involves shelving a project The Sims team has been working on for years: Project Rene, AKA Project Lotus, AKA the nebulous next entry in The Sims franchise, which appears to be some kind of weird Sims MMO mobile game thing. Instead, EA will be focusing on Project Evergreen, which is rumored to be a sort of remaster of The Sims 4, with all (or most) DLC packs included, and recurring bugs squashed.

"We're supporting this franchise by pausing work on one of the next titles in this franchise" doesn't exactly inspire confidence, especially after the nonchalance with which EA just killed two other beloved game franchises. But I think this actually might be the right move.

It's been a bumpy couple of years for The Sims, and many players aren't particularly enthused about Project Rene/Lotus, as it seems to be once again trying to recreate The Sims Online, something EA has tried to rebuild over and over . In fact, much of the reason The Sims 4 launched in such awful shape was due to the fact that it was initially meant to be an MMO-style game that could run on mobile devices. Less than a year before launch, EA pivoted to a more traditional Sims game--but by then, so much of the game had been built with online play and mobile devices in mind that it was too late to turn back. Despite releasing over 100 DLC packs and embarking on a concentrated campaign to squash the game's many, many, many bugs , longtime Sims players are still frustrated with the state of The Sims 4, often pointing out the numerous ways it pales in comparison to its predecessor, The Sims 3.

The Sims 4 is officially "done" in that there are no plans to release any more expansion packs for the game. When it comes to the future of the franchise, most players don't want the next Sims title to be yet another attempt at shoehorning online and/or mobile gameplay into a game that is, at its core, all about building and playing with digital dolls in their digital dollhouses. So EA's decision to hit pause on Project Rene/Lotus's development isn't something I find especially heartbreaking. In fact, I think it's the first truly wise decision EA's made regarding the franchise in a long time, provided EA actually plans to support Project Evergreen long-term (which the name Evergreen would suggest).

Sims 4 players don't want Project Rene, but they do want either The Sims 5 or a complete, playable version of The Sims 4--ideally one that doesn't require the purchase of $1,600 in DLC packs to feel "finished." Hitting pause on its weird, experimental Sims projects in favor of attempting to preserve The Sims 4 in a stable, playable, "evergreen" state is arguably the best decision EA could make, given the current state of both EA and The Sims franchise. Pouring resources into a concept that has failed before (online MMO-style Sims gameplay) rather than a tried-and-true formula (a digital dollhouse) would only harm the franchise at this point.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Rene.png?w=636

Of course, there's no telling what kind of shape Project Evergreen will launch in, assuming it does successfully make it to launch. It sounds like the Evergreen devs have a deadline to hit--hence the reshuffling of resources away from Rene/Lotus--but even with the increase in development resources, there's no guarantee Evergreen will be a massive hit with players.

Provided the rest of development does go smoothly and Evergreen is indeed well-received by players, it may still fall short of EA's goals when it comes to profits. EA has spent the last decade doing everything possible to monetize the living hell out of The Sims 4, a game that--unlike EA's lucrative sports catalog--is largely intended to be a solitary gaming experience that doesn't require online play. Back in the olden days of The Sims 1, 2, and 3, players would purchase the base game, a few expansion packs, and maybe a couple of "stuff packs" for extra decor options, but that was all one really needed to enjoy the game.

The Sims 4, however, introduced an era of seemingly endless DLC: expansion packs, game packs, stuff packs, kits--there are over 100 of them, ranging in cost from $40 to $5, and totaling around $1,600 if purchased individually outside of sales and bundles. In addition to the constant stream of DLC releases, EA has in recent years implemented daily login rewards, various events and challenges, and even a paid mod store nobody asked for --all in the hopes of getting players to spend more time and money on The Sims 4. For a while there, I half-expected EA to implement a Sims 4 battle pass.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Gardening.png?w=636

There's no telling what sort of irritating monetization tactics we'll see in Project Evergreen, but at the very least, Evergreen sounds like an attempt to try and maintain the series' roots, rather than continue chasing the mobile MMO Roblox-like direction Project Lotus seemed to be taking. Even better, Evergreen may turn out to be the game Sims players have been aching for since The Sims 4 launched to middling reviews back in 2014: a game that isn't fundamentally broken and lacking in content.

The real question is if Evergreen will be successful enough to keep The Sims franchise alive. Given that EA's new owners were happy to kill off what was shaping up to be a potentially great Mass Effect game , it's not hard to imagine a world where the Grim Reaper inevitably comes for The Sims, regardless of whether players love or hate Project Evergreen. After all, feelings don't generate dollar signs, and EA's new owners have made one thing abundantly clear: killing off an iconic franchise is "worth it" if it saves EA a few Simoleons.

items.title: Sam Altman 认为，实际上，你希望计算机中使用 DRAM 而不是数据中心，这很糟糕
items.summary: Once again, we're all fuming about big tech and AI.

content.v: More and more, AI appears to be the reason we can't have nice things on the internet. Beyond generative models gobbling up my own and my fellow creatives' work in a bid to produce abysmally average output, AI data centres are also devouring all of the available memory. This drives up prices and makes DRAM supply for us PC gamers pretty scarce . CEO of OpenAI Sam Altman argues this is truly for the best.

Appearing on a recent episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast , Altman argued, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time."

Yes, that is steam escaping from my ears. But before I go full screaming tea kettle, let's take a beat. Altman is talking less about PC gamers specifically here, and more about solo AI bros craving compute power and "local inference".

He's bemoaning an inefficiency within the AI industry rather than taking aim at us pesky gamers. He goes on to add, "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow everyone's... Many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

It still feels a bit rich for Altman to complain about the memory scarcity OpenAI and ChatGPT helped create. I could also keyboard warrior my way through several paragraphs about how resource hungry the data centres he's arguing should enjoy DRAM priority are, not to mention how the rapid AI infrastructure build out has caused many of big tech's greener energy goals to fall by the wayside —but I'll spare you. Our planet's environmental predicament doesn't begin or end with Sam Altman or OpenAI, after all.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bKdvxF2aTyA54pkbpasntQ-1920-80.jpg

Instead, I'm choosing to extract a grim sense of satisfaction from the AI snake eating its own tail. For one thing, Google's AI features appear to be cannibalising ad revenue from search . For another, Amazon's big data centre build out has made free cash flow negative , and for just one more thing, investors haven't been overjoyed with the recent performance of many AI stocks, leading to a big sell-off earlier this month .
The bubble may not have burst yet, but the aforementioned snake is looking a little green around the scales.

items.title: 据报道，EA 已将 BioWare 和质量效应 5 转而制作新的《星球大战：前线》
items.summary: One last bitter drop in a chalice of sorrow.

others.title: New Mass Effect Cancelled So EA Can Focus on Star Wars Battlefront 3

content.v: According to Bloomberg's sources, EA saw a new Battlefront game as a less risky investment than Mass Effect Universe. This final factor joined a host of well-discussed reasons for BioWare's unfortunate demise: Andromeda's critical reception, Anthem's live service failure, Veilguard's sales struggle ( pretty good game though ), friction between the studio and EA since the very beginning, and, of course, EA's recent Saudi-Kushner-Private Equity acquisition.

One other added wrinkle: BioWare apparently lost its main ally at the top of the EA org chart. Entertainment and Central Development exec Laura Miele, who historically advocated for BioWare, was "sidelined" according to Bloomberg. EA sports execs David Tinson and Cam Weber were promoted instead. The age of nerds has ended, now begins the long night of the jock.

Overall, this new information doesn't radically reframe BioWare's overall story at EA, one of slow decline and mismanagement, or how most observers will interpret it through a culture war lens⁠. Was BioWare too woke? Not woke enough? For the love of god keep it out of our comments section. But now we know why the knife was finally driven home, for what it's worth.

And I guess we can anticipate a new Battlefront game some time at the tail end of the 2030s. Woohoo. For more on the closure of BioWare, PCG lead SEO editor Lauren Morton spoke to 16 developers who were inspired to join the industry because of the studio about what BioWare meant to them.
