items.title: 《使命召唤：现代战争 2》评级可能会泄露 2009 年原版 FPS 的端口
items.summary: The Australian Classification Board has rated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, suggesting a port of Infinity Wa

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/07/19/call-of-duty-ambience-lobbies-1784502331743.png
The Australian Classification Board has rated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 , suggesting a port of Infinity Ward's original 2009 shooter may soon be revealed.

The ACB updated its website to reflect a fresh R 18+ rating for the fan-favorite entry in the Activision franchise, with a classification date of October 1, 2026, as spotted by Insider Gaming . Reflecting a mature description based on instances of "high-impact drug use, in-game purchases, online interactivity and chat," the sudden appearance of a rating suggests Microsoft may have plans to revisit Modern Warfare 2 in the near future.

The page, which is still live at the time of this piece's publication, specifically calls the title "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009)." As many others have already pointed out, the obvious assumption is that this is our first hint that a proper port will soon be revealed. Which platforms it may appear on was not shared, but fans may want to stay on their toes for an announcement.

There is one major reason to suspect Modern Warfare 2 (2009) may soon return: Activision tried the same strategy with the Black Ops series earlier this year. Ports for Black Ops 1 and 2 were leaked , announced , and launched all within the span of about one month back in June – and seemingly to much success. Black Ops 2, specifically, reportedly emerged as one of the best-selling games of the year in the month after its launch, but Activision's decision to replay its hits didn't arrive without controversy.

Many criticized the Call of Duty ports as "low effort," calling out both Black Ops games for being little more than direct rips of the original 2010s releases with few, if any, upgrades. There was also the issue of exploiters, as multiplayer lobbies quickly populated with players more interested in taking advantage of the level-up system than actually playing the game . Activision eventually looked into the issue .

While tech and gameplay problems soured an otherwise exciting moment for Call of Duty fans, both ports' prices didn't do the release any favors either. Each game cost $40 on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. DLC was also sold separately, with fans of the add-on content asked to spend $29.99 for each season pass if they didn't want to purchase any content individually. Discounts for PlayStation Plus subscribers helped soften the blow, but players will probably be on the lookout for similar issues should a Modern Warfare 2 port pop up.

Microsoft and Activision brought both Black Ops 1 and 2 ports exclusively to PlayStation consoles in July. Which platforms Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) may launch for, or if ports for other early entries in the Modern Warfare series will show up, remains to be seen. We'll have to wait for Activision to confirm the news to learn more.

IGN gave Infinity Ward's 2009 Call of Duty game a 9.5/10 review upon its release. For more, you can read about the developer who said it was "hard to watch" Xbox profit from its recent Black Ops ports . You can also check out the ambience website that lets you fall asleep to the sound of old-school CoD lobbies .

items.title: 《COD：现代战争》在强烈反对后将削减现实生活中的韩国悲剧部分
items.summary: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfa

content.v: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update.

The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon. Approximately 100,000 people gathered in a narrow alleyway in Seoul, resulting in 160 casualties as people were suffocated. This year marks the fourth anniversary of the tragedy, with bereaved families and community organizers gathering to remember the lives that were lost.

Modern Warfare 4 hit consoles and PC on October 23, and not long after its release, the game drew criticism from bereaved Korean families. In the opening cutscene to the game's campaign--which focuses on a fictional war between North and South Korea--Modern Warfare 4 depicts a chaotic scene where one person performs CPR on a downed individual, while bodies are either laid out on the streets or carried away on stretchers. Given the game's setting and the events on screen, the 10.29 Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and the Citizens' Countermeasures Meeting--two organizations formed after the 2022 tragedy in Seoul--were "appalled" at the calamity's inclusion and demanded that Activision remove it from the game.

"Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC . "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures."

Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. In responding to the criticism , Activision said it never intended to trivialize the disaster or make light of human suffering.

"In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilises some real-world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative," Activision said. "It is not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form."

items.title: 《幻刃零式》的首席配音演员似乎在最后一刻被替换
items.summary: There's a new voice behind the protagonist of Soul in Phantom Blade Zero , and it's none other than Sonic the

content.v: There's a new voice behind the protagonist of Soul in Phantom Blade Zero , and it's none other than Sonic the Hedgehog--or his longtime voice actor, Roger Craig Smith, to be precise.

As spotted by Game Informer , Smith has stepped in to replace Jay Maksenuk (V in Once Human). You can still hear the latter in the various trailers for Phantom Blade Zero, and developer S-Game hasn't revealed why they brought Smith on as a last-minute replacement. Both actors have several video game credits, and as Game Informer noted, it sounds like Masenuk was replaced shortly after the game's review period began. Essentially, you won't be hearing Masenuk's voice, as the game launched earlier this week with Craig voicing the main character.

You're probably familiar with Craig's voice; in addition to Sonic and Batman, he's also voiced Ezio Auditore in several Assassin's Creed games, Daigo Dojima in Yakuza Kiwami 3, and Alden Dorne in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. As a friendly reminder, set a hard limit on how much coffee Smith consumes if you're thinking of interviewing him.

Phantom Blade Zero has had a strong launch week so far, reaching over 730,000 concurrent players on Steam at the time of writing. If you're planning to play this weekend, check out our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub for dozens of walkthroughs, and if you're still on the fence, read our Phantom Blade Zero review to see if it's for you. You can also learn how it fixes one of the biggest problems of soulslike-inspired boss fights.
